result.summary: This pull request harmonizes data directory resolution between GUI and CLI tools. When a user selects a custom data directory in the GUI intro screen, Bitcoin Core creates a symlink (or a text file fallback on unsupported filesystems) at the default datadir location pointing to the selected directory. In addition, `bitcoin-wallet` is updated to load configuration files from the datadir for parity with other CLI binaries.
result.problem: When users select a custom data directory in the GUI, the path is stored in platform-specific Qt settings that CLI tools ignore. Consequently, `bitcoind`, `bitcoin-cli`, and `bitcoin-wallet` default to `~/.bitcoin`, causing blocks to be downloaded to the wrong location, missing wallet files, and broken CLI commands.

resolved_concerns: luke-jr asked whether this would break reading bitcoin.conf placed in the GUI-selected datadir; the author confirmed config file reading is retained.

result.card: PR #27409 makes CLI tools and the GUI share the same data directory setting by placing a symlink or pointer file at the default datadir path when a custom directory is chosen in the GUI intro dialog. It solves the long-standing bug where CLI tools ignore GUI-configured paths and operate on a separate directory, potentially misplacing wallet and block data. It also updates the offline bitcoin-wallet tool to load config files from the datadir. The PR is currently paused as the author indicated difficulty completing comprehensive Qt test coverage across configuration states, and the branch needs a rebase.
